of the China Printing and Finishing Company originated

Chapel. He was previously dismissed on March 29, 1938,

leaving the plant before the proper hour. He was,
however, re-engaged on the following day, presumably
in order to avoid extensive labour trouble. His final
dismissal was preceeded by three warnings for general
misbehaviour and efforts to instigate employees to
declare a strike.

事由：中国印染整理公司浦东厂劳资纠纷。
制作人：D.S. Hide 转呈人：C. Crawford 警佐

中国印染整理公司浦东厂目前的劳资纠纷始于1939年5月20日（星期六）上午9时30分左右，起因是解雇了名为顾金根（Koo Kyung Kung）的3号电工，该员约26岁，上海籍，最后已知住址为江湾路查佩尔（Chapel，音译）金口路3号。他此前曾于1938年3月29日因停止织布厂马达运行并在规定时间前离开工厂而被解雇。然而，他于次日被重新录用，推测是为了避免大范围的劳工麻烦。他的最终解雇之前，曾因一般行为不端及企图煽动员工罢工而受到三次警告。

在他被解雇后，顾金根显然按照预谋计划，与大约80名机械工人员工取得联系，这些人随即停止并封锁了全厂所有电动马达，导致生产完全停滞。

由于全体员工因此闲置，以顾金根为首的一批男性煽动者趁机在厂区内举行了一系列会议，并鼓动工人宣布罢工。

全天管理层都试图通过与工人选出的多个代表团进行谈判来解决纠纷，但是，由于少数煽动者的持续努力，以及

使得立即解决成为不可能。由于时间已晚，管理层随后集中精力试图说服工人和平离开，并承诺将在5月22日（星期一）对通过正式任命的代表提交的合理投诉给予充分考虑。随后，煽动者再次施加压力，强行阻止工人离开厂区。

在这些谈判过程中，大约18至20名外籍职员站在工厂办公室外，逐渐被800至1000名华籍员工包围。下午6时30分左右，一批男性煽动者手持铁条，在顾金根的率领下对外籍职员发起攻击。在随后的争斗中，J. Wallis Chapman 先生头部被铁条击中倒地，另有两三名外国人及几名罢工者受轻伤。

此时局势变得十分严峻，外籍职员退入工厂办公室，但暴民随即冲击办公室，成功对办公场所和设备造成了严重破坏。他们最终闯入办公室，并再次对外国人发动攻击。

with a pistol kept on the premises for protective
purposes and deliberately fired one shot above the
heads of the attackers who then retired and formed
into small groups about the compound.
In the meanwhile, one member of the foreign staff
had made a surreptitious departure from the premises
for the purpose of making an appeal to the British
Consulate for assistance in the protection of British
lives and property, as a result of which a detachment
of sailors from H.M.S. Decoy was landed on the mill
premises at about 8.00 p.m.. The operatives then
dispersed and proceeded to Shanghai by the Company's
sampans.
Mr. J. Wallis Chapman was subsequently removed to
hospital where he was detained for treatment until
Thursday, May 25, 1939.
Negotiations having failed to bring about a
settlement of the dispute, the management decided to
close the plant and pay-off the entire staff. The
pay-off commenced at the Company's offices at 220,
Szechuen Road, at 9.30 a.m. on Tuesday, May 23, and
was continued during office hours until Saturday,
May 27, when all save 150 of the 2,000 operatives had
received their wages.
Various foreign employees who were present during
the disturbance have since identified photographs of

与此同时，一名外籍职员秘密离开工厂，前往英国领事馆请求协助保护英国人的生命和财产，结果 HMS Decoy 号（皇家海军迪科伊号）的一队水兵于晚上8时左右登陆工厂厂区。工人们随后散去，乘坐公司的舢板前往上海。
J. Wallis Chapman 先生随后被送往医院，留院治疗直至1939年5月25日（星期四）。
由于谈判未能解决纠纷，管理层决定关闭工厂并遣散全体员工。遣散工作于5月23日（星期二）上午9时30分在公司位于四川路220号的办事处开始，并在办公时间内持续进行，直至5月27日（星期六），当时2000名工人中除150人外均已领取工资。
骚乱期间在场的多名外籍雇员此后指认了以下员工的照片，确认他们积极参与了煽动活动以及对 J. Wallis Chapman 先生等人的袭击。

In an effort to effect the arrest of these
persons, foreign and Chinese detectives from the
Special Branch and Central Station maintained
observation at the Company's offices during the pay-
off of the employees. At 9.30 a.m. on May 25,
detectives identified one Woo Siau Nyeu (serial number
7 of the persons described above) who was discreetly
followed and arrested outside the premises.

In the attached statement, Woo Siau Nyeu denies
having taken part in the disturbance, alleging that
at the time he was in the boiler room cooking his
food and washing his clothes. He has been detained
pending the result of further enquiries.

The China Printing and Finishing Company has
announced that the Pootung plant will be re-opened
on Monday, May 29, 1939.

It should be noted that the reports appearing
in the Chinese press alleging the strike to be the
outcome of a dispute between a Russian watchman and
a Chinese female operative are incorrect. In order
to minimize the possibility of an operative falling
overboard, the Russian watchman employed on the
premises have instructions to effect strict supervision
over the employees when they embark and disembark on
the Company's sampans which convey them to and from
the Shanghai side. Objections to this ruling have
been made from time to time, but the management

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Woo Siao Nan ( 吳 小 南 )
native of Liyang taken by me
at Special Branch on the 25-5-39 and interpreted by Clerk Loh Wei Kong

My name is Woo Siao Nan, age 27, native of Liyang,
single. I came to Shanghai in March, 1938 and worked as
a porter on the various wharves at Pootung, until July,
1938 when I secured employment in the Pootung Mill of the
China Printing and Finishing Company through the introduction
of Wong Soo-yu ( 王 素 餘 ), who is a coolie foreman engaged
in transporting coal for the company.

I am a coolie engaged in painting glass at a
monthly pay of some $20.00 which was usually issued once
every two weeks. I worked about ten hours a day, i.e.
from 7 a.m. to 12 noon, and from 12.20 p.m. to 6 p.m.
Up to May 20, I was living on the premises of the mill.

At 6 p.m. May 20, when I had finished working, I
saw about 1,000 male and female day shift workers
congregated in the mill yard, and heard a number of them
shouting to their colleagues to cease operations and stop
the machines, and threatening to assault those who attempted
to work, but I was ignorant as to the cause of the strike.
I then went to the boiler room for the purpose of cooking
food and washing my clothing as I usually did. After
finishing my supper at about 8 p.m., I came out from the
boiler room and found the majority of the workers had left
the mill premises, so I followed them out of the mill and
came to this side by ferry, which stopped at the Customs
Jetty near Hankow Road. I proceeded alone to the
Roosevelt Terminal and returned to Pootung and passed
that night in the home of my friend named Siao Tu Tse

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警方调查报告。

以下为吴小南（Woo Siao Nan，即吴小南）的供词，该员系溧阳人，由我于1939年5月25日在特务科录取，由书记员罗伟公（Loh Wei Kong，音译）翻译。

我叫吴小南，27岁，溧阳人，未婚。我于1938年3月来到上海，在浦东各码头担任搬运工，直到1938年7月，通过为公司运煤的苦力领班王素余（Wong Soo-yu，音译）的介绍，我在中国印染整理公司浦东厂找到了工作。

我是一名负责玻璃涂漆的苦力，月薪约20元，通常每两周发放一次。我每天工作约十小时，即上午7时至中午12时，以及下午12时20分至6时。截至5月20日，我一直居住在工厂厂区内。

5月20日下午6时，我下班后，看到约1000名男女日班工人聚集在工厂院子里，听到其中一些人向同事喊话，要求停止作业和机器运转，并威胁要殴打那些试图工作的人，但我不知道罢工的起因。随后，我像往常一样去锅炉房做饭和洗衣服。晚上8点左右吃完晚饭后，我从锅炉房出来，发现大多数工人已经离开工厂厂区，于是我跟随他们离开工厂，乘渡轮来到这边，渡轮在靠近汉口路的海关码头停靠。我独自前往罗斯福码头（Roosevelt Terminal），返回浦东，并在我的朋友小杜子（Siao Tu Tse，音译）家中过夜

On the morning of May 21, I again came to this

(吴漢高), who is my fellow countryman and a wharf
coolie foreman residing at House No.3 Mei Foh Li (茂福里),

During the evening of May 24, I was informed by

I have no knowledge of the cause of the present
strike, nor did I take an active part in it. I am at a

REPORT
File No. POLICE REGISTRY
Date May 27, 1939.
Subject China Printing and Finishing Company - Strike situation
in Pootung Mill
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The strike situation in the Pootung Mill of
the China Printing and Finishing Company remains
unchanged.

Information obtained from the female workers
of the mill show that on May 24 and 25, members of
the Bureau of Social Affairs of the "Shanghai City
Government" secretly approached several mill employees
and urged upon them to persist in the strike and
promised to issue them the sum of $1.00 each and
$20.00 to each ringleader provided they register
with the authorities, but the workers are said to
be undecided in their attitude towards the offer.

It is also reported that the mill intends
re-opening on May 29.

With reference to the remarks of the D.C.
(Special Branch) in respect of the agitation carried
out by strikers of the China Printing and Finishing
Company coercing other British owned concerns in the
Settlement, discreet enquiries have been carried out
at several British firms and are being continued by
the staff of this office, but so far no sign of any
approach has been found with the exception of the
Yee Tsoong Tobacco Factory at Pootung.

The present strike in the China Printing and
Finishing Company and the reported assistance rendered
by the Japanese authorities and pro-Japanese
organizations to the strikers is said to have aroused

主题 中国印染公司——浦东工厂罢工局势
制作及呈报人：督察长克劳福德（D.I. Crawford）

中国印染公司浦东工厂的罢工局势保持不变。

从该厂女工处获得的情报显示，5月24日和25日，“上海市政府”社会局的成员秘密接触了几名工厂员工，敦促他们坚持罢工，并承诺只要向当局登记，每人将发给1.00元，每名头目发给20.00元，但据说工人们对该提议的态度尚不确定。

另有报告称，该厂打算于5月29日重新开工。

关于特别课副督察长（D.C. (Special Branch)）就中国印染公司罢工者胁迫租界内其他英资企业一事所作的评语，已在几家英商公司进行了谨慎的调查，并由本办公室人员继续进行，但截至目前，除浦东的颐中烟草厂（Yee Tsoong Tobacco Factory）外，未发现任何接触的迹象。

据悉，中国印染公司目前的罢工以及日本当局和亲日组织向罢工者提供援助的报道，已引起

the interest of the employees of the Yee Tsoong

took place during the afternoon of May 25 in
connection with a demand for an increase in wages.
The unrest came to the notice of the management
later who summoned the foremen in the various
departments to the office of the Managing Director
on the morning of May 26 and ordered them to inform
the workers that a 15% wage increase would be granted
in the near future.

At about 2.30 p.m., May 25, a dynamo exploded
in the power plant of the Yee Tsoong Tobacco Factory
at Pootung, due to the negligence of two electricians.
This damage resulted in the suspension of work in the
Leaf Department, the Motor Room, etc., and affected
a total of some 3,000 operatives. The management
issued a notice granting a holiday on May 29 to the
workers of the Tin Foil Room and the Cigarette Box
Making Room, as the repairs to the motor will require
a fairly lengthy period.

Enquiries among the labourers of the Ewo
Cotton Mill (670 Yangtszepoo Road) and the Yangtszepoo
Cotton Mill (1056 Yangtszepoo Road), two of the
British owned concerns which have been visited, show
that they are more or less satisfied with their
present treatment. There are some 5,000 operatives
in the employ of each mill on day and night shifts.

5月25日下午2时30分左右，由于两名电工的疏忽，浦东颐中烟草厂发电厂的发电机发生爆炸。此次损坏导致叶片部、电机房等部门停工，共影响约3,000名操作工。鉴于电机维修需要相当长的时间，管理层发布通知，给予锡箔部和烟盒制造部的工人5月29日放假。

对已走访的两家英资企业——怡和纱厂（Ewo Cotton Mill，杨树浦路670号）和杨树浦纱厂（Yangtszepoo Cotton Mill，杨树浦路1056号）的劳工进行的调查显示，他们对目前的待遇大致满意。每家工厂昼夜两班倒雇用的操作工约有5,000人。

REPORT

Subject Strike of workers of the China Printing & Finishing Works,
Pootung - present situation

Made by D. I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C. Crawford. O. I.

Between 2 p.m. and 5 p.m., on May 24, 1939,
some 600 workers of the China Printing & Finishing Works,
Pootung, who are on strike, gathered at the Pootung
Southern District Administrative Office, Tung Chong
Road, Pootung, where they received from Mr. Hashimoto
( 橋本 ), Chief of the Pootung Section of the
Japanese Military Special Service Department, 100
coppers each as "Relief Fee". A sum of $30.00
each was issued to the seven wounded workers as
medical expenses. And after payment, an official
of the Pootung Southern District Administrative
Office announced that a further amount would be
issued to the workers next Monday morning. Some
300 sentries were posted in the vicinity of the
Pootung plant of the China Printing & Finishing
Works, by the Japanese Military between the hours of
6 a.m. and 9 a.m., when they were withdrawn.

Information to hand shows that one third of the
workers of the Paillienking plant of the China Printing
& Finishing Works are already on a "Tai Kung" Strike
and that it is expected that the remainder will
follow their example.

Huge quantities of anti-British posters were
found posted on walls along Tung Chong Road, Pootung,
and it is reported that those posters were pasted up
by members of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai City

报告

主题 浦东中国印染厂工人罢工——当前局势

制作人：督察潘连璧（D. I. Pan Lien Pih） 呈报人：首席督察克劳福德（C. Crawford. O. I.）

1939年5月24日下午2时至5时之间，约600名正在罢工的中国印染厂浦东工厂工人聚集在浦东同宗路（Tung Chong Road）的浦东南区行政公署，从日本军方特务机关浦东分部主任桥本（Hashimoto）先生处领取每人100枚铜板作为“救济费”。七名受伤工人每人获发30.00元作为医疗费。发放完毕后，浦东南区行政公署的一名官员宣布，下周一早晨将向工人发放更多款项。上午6时至9时期间，日军在中国印染厂浦东工厂附近部署了约300名哨兵，随后撤走。

现有情报显示，中国印染厂百炼精（Paillienking）分厂已有三分之一的工人正在进行“怠工”（Tai Kung）罢工，预计其余工人也将效仿。
